simple.meaning: מְשֹׁל (mᵉshôl) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a satire.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Job, beginning at Job 17:6. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְשֹׁל (H4914) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מְשֹׁל (mᵉshôl) / H4914 is traced through Job 17:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4914. meshol מְשֹׁל noun [masculine] by-word , only construct (strictly Infinitive) עַמִּים לִמְשֹׁל Job 17:6 (they) have made me a by-word of the peoples.

occurrences.englishText: “But he has made me a byword of the people.
